Unlike other integrations modified in this PR, Salesforce does not use the new `refreshOAuthTokens` helper, so even when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, Salesforce will still refresh directly using the locally stored `credentialKey.refresh_token` rather than delegating to the sync endpoint. This is a concrete, diff-grounded inconsistency and potential performance/regression concern, though whether it is strictly a correctness bug depends on intended requirements not shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:25 — The check `req.headers[...] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` passes when the secret env var is not defined and the request has no header (`undefined !== undefined` is false). An unauthenticated caller can then write credentials for any userId, unless APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED also requires the secret to be set. That constant's definition is not in this diff, so the guard cannot be confirmed (P0, conf 50)

adjudication.rationale: The diff *does* define `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` in `packages/lib/constants.ts` as `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY;`. In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler immediately returns 403 when this constant is falsy, so the scenario `undefined !== undefined` (both header and secret missing) cannot occur because the route is already blocked when `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is not set. When the secret is set, a missing header yields `undefined !== <secret>` and correctly denies access.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:25 — The webhook secret is compared with plain `!==` instead of `crypto.timingSafeEqual`, and there is no check for a minimum length or a non-empty value. The response time leaks how much of the secret matched, so the secret can be recovered byte by byte through the only auth gate on an endpoint that overwrites any user's stored OAuth credentials (P2, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the auth gate is a direct header-to-secret comparison using `!==` (lines around the `req.headers[...] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` check). This is not constant-time and can leak match progress via timing differences. The endpoint then proceeds to decrypt and `update`/`create` credentials for an arbitrary `userId` from the request body, so this comparison is the only protection before overwriting stored OAuth credentials. Additionally, there is no explicit minimum-length validation for `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`/header value beyond `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` being truthy, so very short secrets are allowed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:58 — `symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || "")` falls back to an empty key instead of failing closed. A missing encryption key does not stop the endpoint; decryption just runs with an empty key. Also, `JSON.parse` of the decrypted output is written straight into `credential.key` with no schema check, so whoever holds the secret can store any JSON as any app's credential (P2, conf 50)

adjudication.rationale: The claim that a missing CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY “does not stop the endpoint” is not supported by the diff: the handler gates on `if (!APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED) return 403`, and `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is defined as `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, so an unset/empty encryption key makes the endpoint reject before decryption. However, the second issue is real in this diff: `const keys = JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` is written directly into `prisma.credential.update/create` as `key: keys` with no app-specific schema validation/sanitization, so any caller who knows the webhook secret (and encryption key, given the gate) can store arbitrary JSON as the credential payload for any existing `userId` and any `appSlug` present in `appStoreMetadata`, which is a data-integrity/security defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:6 — The credential-sync POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT carries no authentication (no shared secret or signature header), and the response is trusted as fresh tokens under a looser schema (`minimumTokenResponseSchema`). The parent app cannot tell Cal.com apart from anyone else asking for a user's access token by calcomUserId, and Cal.com stores whatever the endpoint (or anyone intercepting a non-TLS URL) returns (P2, conf 50)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `refreshOAuthTokens` which, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, performs a POST to `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` with only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` in the body and no authentication material (no shared secret, signature, or auth header): `fetch(..., { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams({ calcomUserId, appSlug }) })`. Separately, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` explicitly relaxes validation under the same conditions by using `minimumTokenResponseSchema` instead of the app-specific schema, accepting essentially any response with an `access_token` and some numeric expiry field. This combination makes the sync endpoint callable without Cal.com proving its identity, and makes Cal.com accept/store token refresh results under a weaker schema when sync is enabled—both are directly evidenced by the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 — No test exercises the refresh path: `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)` returns the safeParse wrapper `{ success, data }`, not the parsed data that `googleCredentialSchema.parse` used to return, so `data: { key }` writes a malformed credential on every refresh; one test asserting the persisted key shape would catch it (P1, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)` returns the Zod `safeParse` result object (`{ success, data, error }`), not the parsed token data itself. In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refresh path now does `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and then persists it via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. That writes the wrapper object into `credential.key` rather than the expected credential payload shape (previously `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` returned the payload). This is a concrete, diff-verifiable correctness defect that would corrupt stored refreshed credentials.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — The new sync-mode branch has no test: `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` evaluates to the literal key "[object Object]", which the next line then overwrites, so the "minimum" schema strips `expiry_date`/`expires_in` and never checks for any expiry field; a single safeParse test would show the schema does not do what its comment says (P1, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined with computed keys `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()`. These evaluate to fixed literal property names (whatever `.toString()` returns), not “any key with a number value” / “allow other properties” as the comments claim. As a result, the schema will not actually validate common expiry fields like `expiry_date`/`expires_in` in the sync-mode branch (`minimumTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(response)`), and will likely reject otherwise valid token responses or fail to enforce the intended expiry requirement. This is a concrete behavioral defect in the newly added code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:26 — No test covers the fallback `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`: office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:263 spreads that data over `o365AuthCredentials`, so a refresh response without refresh_token replaces the stored real token with the literal string "refresh_token", and future refreshes break silently (P1, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, if the parsed token response lacks `refresh_token`, the code forcibly sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`. In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refreshed response is parsed via `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)` and then merged into persisted credentials with `o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) }`. When credential syncing is enabled (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` + `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`), `parseRefreshTokenResponse` uses `minimumTokenResponseSchema` (which does not require `refresh_token`), so the fallback injects the literal string and the spread overwrites the real stored refresh token. That is a verifiable correctness/data-loss bug that will cause subsequent refresh attempts to use the bogus refresh token.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5 — The sync branch (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`) is untested and returns a raw fetch `Response`, but googlecalendar reads `res?.data` and hubspot uses it directly as `HubspotToken`, so in sync mode both callers get undefined or wrong-shaped tokens and nothing verifies what each caller expects back (P1, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, the sync branch returns the raw `fetch(...)` `Response` object. Multiple callers shown in the diff expect non-`fetch` response shapes: e.g. Google Calendar does `const token = res?.data;` after calling `refreshOAuthTokens(...)`, but a `fetch` Response has no `.data` property, so `token` becomes `undefined` in sync mode and subsequent `token.access_token` access will break. Hubspot assigns the return value to `HubspotToken` (`const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)`), but in sync mode it would be a `Response`, not a `HubspotToken`, causing wrong-shaped token usage. The diff contains no adaptation/parsing in `refreshOAuthTokens` to normalize the return type for callers.
